definition: The traditions the family tree does not hold. Japanese, Islamic, South Asian and African building would each be a peer trunk beside the traditions it does hold, and the schema extends to them without modification.
more: One absence is already visible inside the tree: Cape Dutch carries an acknowledged gap, because its Cape and Indonesian strand has no node to point at.
basis: The corpus's own account of what it leaves out, reworded. README.md, under what remains: "Japanese, Islamic, South Asian, and African traditions would each be a peer trunk, and the schema extends to them without modification." and "Cape Dutch already carries an acknowledged gap: its Cape and Indonesian strand has no node to point at." Which traditions the tree does hold is not written here: the page derives it from the tree it has in hand, the nodes whose rank is a tradition.
